walkthroughs.title: Cancelling, and what does not change afterwards

moments.say: Alice cancels; billing stops, she keeps access, and she gets an email.
She presses cancel again, and nothing changes.
She asks for a refund of the unused part of the period and is turned down.
The paid period ends and her access ends with it.
A refund is still turned down.

walkthroughs.goal: Alice cancels, presses cancel again, and asks for money back.

walkthroughs.title: The provider does not cooperate

moments.say: Bob cancels, but the provider does not answer in time; he is still subscribed and billed.
A second try gets no answer either.
A third try is declined by the provider. Bob is still subscribed, and the count of unanswered tries starts over.
The next try goes through, and Bob is told in the app.

walkthroughs.goal: Bob wants to cancel while the billing provider is having a bad day.

walkthroughs.title: Three tries without an answer, no fourth

moments.say: Alice cancels; the provider does not answer.
A second try gets no answer.
Nor does a third. Alice is still subscribed.
A fourth try is not made.

walkthroughs.goal: The provider never answers Alice's cancellation.

journeys.title: Cancelling a subscription

steps.say: The customer cancels; the billing provider accepts and the customer is told.
The paid period ends and access ends with it.

journeys.goal: A customer no longer wants to pay, but has paid for the current period and keeps access until it ends.

assumptions: Two customers (alice, bob) stand for any number; each already has an active subscription.
The billing provider is outside the model: its answer to a cancellation (accepted, declined, no answer) arrives as part of the action.
Refunds are never issued in this area; asking for one is always turned down.
